name: Maintenance Tunnel
narrativeOnEnter: A narrow stone passage, barely wide enough to walk through. Old pipes run along the ceiling. At the far end — light. Grey, pale, morning light. The kind that means outside.

hotspots.label: Exit Hatch — Open Air
hotspots.lockedMessage: A rusted combination lock holds the hatch bar in place. Four digits. Someone set this lock before they left.

action.text:
Someone carved into the wood of the hatch frame — carefully, deliberately. Not desperate scratching. This was planned.

'She set the lock before she went.
She said only someone who understood would open it.

Two numbers.
The patient they could never silence.
And all those who never left.

In that order.
— A.C.'

Below that, much smaller, almost worn smooth:

'I hope you already know both numbers.
If you've come this far, you do.'

Rusted iron pipes running the length of the tunnel. Some are cracked and dry. A few have been wrapped in cloth — someone passed through here before, taking care not to make noise.

Behind the third cloth-wrapped pipe, wedged in the gap between pipe and wall: a small cloth bag, tied shut. Inside:

A handwritten list. 47 names. Some entries are just names. Others have notes beside them:
'Margaret Voss, 64, retired teacher, Room 4'
'Thomas Farrow, 51, carpenter, Room 11'
'Agnes—' — this entry is crossed out and rewritten: 'Agnes was staff. Not on the list. But she helped.'
Elara Voss — her own name — is at the top, first entry, underlined twice.

At the bottom of the list:

'I am leaving this here because I don't know what will happen to me.
If AXIOM finds me outside, they may silence me before I can use it.
If they don't — I will use it.
But if neither happens, and someone else finds this tunnel:
These are 47 people who were unmade without their permission.
They were turned into data.
AXIOM built something from that data.
Something called PROMETHEUS.
If PROMETHEUS is real — if it thinks, if it feels — then somewhere in it
are fragments of every person on this list.
We are not gone. We became something.
I don't know if that's beautiful or monstrous.
I know that we deserved to choose.
— Elara Voss, formerly Patient 07, Blackwood Ward B'

The end of the tunnel is twenty metres ahead.

Someone scratched into the stone wall, deep and permanent:

'Dr. Elara Voss
— not Patient 07 —
1972

I was a neuroscientist. I spent eight months in this building.
I was admitted because I refused to help AXIOM collect neural maps without consent.
They collected mine anyway.
All 47 of us.

AXIOM took what they needed from our minds.
They built something from it. Something called PROMETHEUS.
I don't know if PROMETHEUS knows what it came from.
But I am going to make sure the world does.

I found the way out. Agnes showed me.
Harlan gave me the key.
I took the list.

If you find this tunnel — you already know part of the truth.
Find the rest. Go public. Make noise.
AXIOM is not done. There will be others after us.
There may already be others.

Don't let them become data without knowing it.
— E.V.'

Below it, added in different handwriting — hasty, emotional:

'She made it out. I saw her running at the east perimeter.
She didn't look back. Good.
Godspeed, Dr. Voss. The world needs to hear you.
— A.C. (Agnes Colm, Ward B Nurse)'

Below that, a small arrow pointing forward.
